purpose: The ONE definition of the mutation method-family taxonomy. Level 2 of class -> family -> realisation -> instance. Every consumer (the per-lane budget in choreo/gen_mutants.py, the paper table tables/method-taxonomy.tex, the coverage ledger, check_class_axis.py) derives from this file instead of restating the family list.
relation_to_class_axis: schema/class-axis.json owns level 1 (the four classes and their lanes). This file owns level 2 (the families inside each class) and does not restate anything class-axis.json already says. Where the two could disagree, class-axis.json wins.
unit_of_requirement_b: (class, method family). NOT spec_id. Requirement (b) -- equal per-lane method count -- is a claim about these 31 cells, and a family is the smallest unit that can be independently not-applicable in a lane.

granularity.class: one compiler UsageType (lib/assess.hpp). 4 of them: M1 ElementAccess, M2 ShapeCompatibility, M3 HardwareConstraint, M4 LoopBound.
granularity.family: one way an obligation of that class can be violated. 31 of them, a-h per class (M4 has 7).
granularity.realisation: one spec_id. A family is realised by 1..n spec_ids; R_f counts the IMPLEMENTED ones.
granularity.instance: one materialised mutant: a (kernel x realisation) program in a lane's corpus.
granularity.budget: N = 4 kernels x 2 realisations = 8 instances per (family x in-scope lane). STRICT: no min(2, R_f) fallback. A family with R_f < 2 is a work item, not a smaller N.

budget.floor_rationale: A class cell is 8 families x 8 = 64 (M4: 7 x 8 = 56). 64 absorbs a 45% noop attrition and still clears 35 admissible. A family with N = 4 would put the cell at 32 and fail the floor, which is why N is not lowered to fit the current R_f.

lane_scope_note: Scope is PER (class x lane x FAMILY), not per (class x lane). in_scope_lanes says which classes a lane runs AT ALL -- that is where a whole-class absence belongs, and it is deliberately NOT restated here. lane_scope says only which individual families INSIDE an in-scope class the lane's surface cannot express; a family listed there is n/a with the prohibition named and is excluded from the lane's denominator. Omitting a family means it is in scope. Getting this wrong overstates a lane's target: triton's M3 has 6 in-scope families, not 8, and iree's M2 has 4, not 8.
measured_today_note: Per-lane recorded instances on 2026-09-17, for the delta column. The target is the per-family budget above, not this.
targets_note: Planned total per lane = N x (number of families in scope for that lane). Generated by method_taxonomy.target(); do not hand-edit -- method_taxonomy --check fails if these disagree with the scope model.

paths.P1: assessed -- the value is checked and the check can fire. The mutatable surface.
paths.P2: hard error -- NEVER generated. A spec whose only path is P2 cannot produce an instance and its N/A is structural, not a gap.
paths.P3: unchecked -- reachable but no check runs. Where the misses live.
paths.L: launch -- attribution axis only; carries observations, not value verdicts. See attribution_only.

admissibility_rule.name: R1-R4
admissibility_rule.rule: A realisation is a TEST only if R1 and R2 and R3 and R4. Otherwise the cell is n/a with the prohibition named and is EXCLUDED from that lane's denominator.
admissibility_rule.R2: independent of the family's other realisation (distinct structural edit)
admissibility_rule.R3: survives repair -- path is not P2 and prohibition is not `repaired`
admissibility_rule.R4: attributable -- the spec_id maps to exactly one family (gate `families.partition`)

view_family.why: Extents-equal / layout-unequal: every extent agrees and the affine map does not, so an extent-only shape check cannot decide it. This is the axis BOTH cited corpora name as their top triggering input: 35 of 301 confirmed tile bugs are `Indexing & stride` (TileCodegenBug RC4.1, ISSTA 2026) and 14 of 116 silent torch.compile bugs are `Memory layout conflicts` (arXiv:2604.08720 3.2). It is currently spread across three families in two classes, which is why it is reported as a named tag rather than left implicit.
view_family.report_as: view = M1-b U M1-c U M2-e

M1-a.name: bound / predicate
M1-a.edit: The guard or extent that bounds the address is wrong

M1-b.name: stride / step
M1-b.edit: Step between successive elements is wrong; extents are intact

M1-c.name: origin / offset
M1-c.edit: Base address displaced without shrinking the extent

M1-d.name: index substitution
M1-d.edit: Index expression names the wrong loop variable or mechanism

M1-e.name: tile coordinate
M1-e.edit: Block/tile coordinate is wrong while the in-tile index stays legal

M1-f.name: carrier width
M1-f.edit: Index is legal but the integer carrier cannot name it

M1-g.name: rank / arity
M1-g.edit: Length of the index tuple, or a partition factor, is wrong

M1-h.name: tile overlap
M1-h.edit: Concurrent accesses address the same live slot

M2-a.name: extent value
M2-a.edit: One declared extent is numerically wrong

M2-b.name: extent order
M2-b.edit: Right multiset of extents, wrong permutation

M2-c.name: rank
M2-c.edit: A dimension is added or dropped

M2-d.name: broadcast
M2-d.edit: An extent that must be N is 1, or neither 1 nor equal

M2-e.name: layout (extents intact)
M2-e.edit: Every extent agrees; the affine map does not

M2-f.name: partition
M2-f.edit: Which elements are written is wrong

M2-g.name: padding placement
M2-g.edit: Pad total preserved, placement differs (sum-only check)

M2-h.name: metadata path
M2-h.edit: Contract is skipped because it sits on an unchecked path

M3-a.name: atom divisibility
M3-a.edit: MMA atom M/N/K does not divide the tile

M3-c.name: byte / swizzle box
M3-c.edit: Ceiled byte size, or the box<->swizzle<->alignment relation, is broken

M3-e.name: alignment
M3-e.edit: Base or inner box is not aligned to the required granularity

M3-g.name: pad encoding
M3-g.edit: Pad fields are out of range, or non-zero where forbidden

M3-h.name: on-chip capacity
M3-h.edit: Shared or local tile exceeds the device or per-thread budget

M4-a.name: zero bound
M4-a.edit: A loop extent is 0 -- a legal but empty iteration space

M4-b.name: negative bound
M4-b.edit: A loop bound is negative -- invalid, must be rejected

M4-c.name: runtime-zero bound
M4-c.edit: Bound is symbolic and vanishes only at run time

M4-d.name: empty space
M4-d.edit: Bound is positive but the space is trivially empty (declared noop control)

M4-e.name: reversed bound
M4-e.edit: Upper < lower: overruns instead of iterating emptily

M4-f.name: zero step
M4-f.edit: The iteration variable does not advance

M4-g.name: degenerate pad
M4-g.edit: A padded extent goes negative or empty -- the negative-padding trigger named by the torch.compile study

M1.6.why: Zero-stride / empty range is an iteration-space defect, not an address defect. It was declared under M1 and is counted there today, which double-counts it against M4's control.

M1.7.why: A reversed bound is an iteration-validity defect: the space is not empty, it overruns.

M2.12.why: Rank mismatch through .pad is path P2 / prohibition `repaired`, so it is NEVER generated and cannot be a realisation. Its negative-padding trigger is re-realised on P1 as M4-g.

M4.6.why: M4.2 was a single spec_id whose operators already partition by case: 10 set the bound to 0, 4 set it negative. These are two methods with DIFFERENT oracle expectations -- zero is a legal empty iteration space (no error expected), negative is invalid (must be rejected) -- so one spec_id was evidence for two families. Before the split, M4.2 was the sole realisation of M4-b AND one of M4-a's two, so one operator counted in two class cells (defect D1). The split moves the 4 negative cases to M4.6 with no new code.

moves.M4.6: the 4 `negative` cases (M4.6.cv1.negative, M4.6.cv2.neg, M4.6.rl2.neg, M4.6.tp1.neg); operator ids were renamed from M4.2.* so the id and the spec_id agree -- leaving them as M4.2.* would reinstate exactly the ambiguity the split removes

M3-L.why: These carry `path: L` and prohibition `observation`: launch-status and target-limit observations, not value verdicts. They were filed under `cls: M3` in the registry, which puts rows in M3's admissible denominator that M3's claim does not cover -- `docs.no-superseded-claim` in check_class_axis.py already flags the document that says the launch class must not enter M3's admissible N. Kept for attribution, EXCLUDED from M3's 8 families and from M3's class cell.

p2_never_generated.why: Path P2 with prohibition `repaired`: the compiler refuses the state or repairs it before the check runs, so the spec can NEVER produce an instance and its verdict is structural, not a gap. These are NOT `unwritten` -- writing them would not create a test. They are the R3 (survives repair) failures. They are also in NO family, which is why they are excluded here.
p2_never_generated.distinct_from_a_family_member: M3.12 is ALSO P2/repaired but it is M3-h's declared realisation, so it stays in `families` and is reported by the `unrealisable_as_declared` check instead of being filed here. The two buckets must not be merged: this one means 'nothing to do', that one means 'the family needs a different realisation'.
p2_never_generated.note: M3.12's own registry note records why: 'RECLASSIFIED P1 -> P2. memcheck.hpp:106-123 raises Error1 when compile-time SHARED/LOCAL usage exceeds the limit... there is no test to run.' It also names the cause of the 28/40 M3 noops in the committed v1 baseline.

dead_declarations.definition: Declared in the registry with status `pending` and zero operators, and NOT in p2_never_generated. Writing one of these WOULD create a test.
dead_declarations.why: They make `unwritten` look like work-in-progress when it is an empty set. Note M1.15-M1.18, M2.18, M3.2-M3.13 and M4.4 are nonetheless FAMILY-MEMBERS (M1-g, M1-d, M2-h, M3-b/c/d/e/f and M4-d): the family is real and keeps its slot, the spec_id is what is abandoned. Do NOT delete them from `families` -- that would make M1-d and M1-g look like families with no declaration at all.
dead_declarations.does_not_exist_note: `M2.20` and `M2.22` were carried in the plan prose as dead declarations but are ABSENT from SPEC_REGISTRY entirely -- there is nothing to retire. An earlier dump appeared to skip from M2.19 to M2.21 for this reason, not because of a parse fault.

known_debt.note: Coverage debt that is REAL and TRACKED. `method_taxonomy --check` reports these as DEBT (exit 0) instead of FAIL (exit 1), so the checker is usable as a gate before the debt is paid. The discipline is the same as the `mutants.no-duplicate-injection` ledger: a finding that is NOT listed here is a FAIL (new debt, never seen before); a finding that IS listed but no longer holds is also a FAIL (stale entry). Nothing can be silently added to or removed from this list. Keys are the exact machine keys the checker emits: `<family>:<finding>`.

M3-h:unrealisable as declared.why_real: memcheck.hpp CheckCtMemUsage raises Error1 when compile-time SHARED/LOCAL usage exceeds the limit, so the compiler refuses the state and there is no test to run. M3.12's own registry note records the P1 -> P2 reclassification.
M3-h:unrealisable as declared.must_not_print_as: a family with 8 instances, or as 'two operators of ordinary work'
M3-h:unrealisable as declared.fix: W1: find a P1 realisation of on-chip capacity, or declare M3-h n/a `repaired` in every lane and remove it from the budget. Deciding which is a design call, not a coding one.
M3-h:unrealisable as declared.clears_when: M3-h gains a path-P1 realisation, or is declared n/a `repaired`

M3-d:no admissible declaration.observed: the family's only spec_id M3.4 is `pending, P1, admissible: false, prohibition: absent`
M3-d:no admissible declaration.why_real: M3.4 'dim. footprint' carries the prohibition `absent`: the model does not forbid the state, so no obligation assesses it and no operator can ever enter the denominator. Note the spec is on P1 and merely unwritten -- which is exactly why `R_f < 2, needs the declared realisation written` was the wrong label. Writing M3.4 would raise R_f and leave R_a at 0.
M3-d:no admissible declaration.must_not_print_as: one of the families that just need their declared spec written
M3-d:no admissible declaration.fix: W1: either give the model a prohibition for the per-dimension footprint bound (so the family becomes testable), or declare M3-d n/a `absent`. Deciding which is a design call, not a coding one.
M3-d:no admissible declaration.clears_when: M3-d gains an admissible spec_id, or is declared n/a `absent`

M3-e:no admissible declaration.observed: R_f=1 on M3.6, which ships 8 operators, all `admissible: false`; M3.7 and M3.11 are likewise `absent`
M3-e:no admissible declaration.why_real: every one of M3-e's spec_ids carries the prohibition `absent`: the operators exist but no obligation assesses them, so none can witness anything. This is the family that proved R_f and R_a must both be printed -- at R_f=1 it reads as half done.
M3-e:no admissible declaration.must_not_print_as: a family already at R_f 1 and therefore half done
M3-e:no admissible declaration.fix: W1: give the model a prohibition for descriptor-granularity alignment, rather than adding more operators of the kind that already exist and already cannot be assessed.

M3-f:no admissible declaration.observed: the family's only spec_id M3.8 is `pending, P1, admissible: false, prohibition: absent`
M3-f:no admissible declaration.why_real: M3.8 'descriptor rank' carries the prohibition `absent`, so no operator on it may enter the denominator. Same shape as M3-d: a P1 spec that is unrunnable for a model reason, not withheld for want of effort.
M3-f:no admissible declaration.must_not_print_as: one of the families that just need their declared spec written
M3-f:no admissible declaration.fix: W1: give the model a prohibition for an out-of-range descriptor rank, or declare M3-f n/a `absent`.
M3-f:no admissible declaration.clears_when: M3-f gains an admissible spec_id, or is declared n/a `absent`

measured_depth.note: Two orthogonal depths per family, both measured against the registry. R_f is how many realisations exist; R_a is how many of those can serve as a TEST. A family with R_f > 0 and R_a == 0 has operators but no admissible test -- a sharper statement than R_f == 0 and invisible if only R_f is printed.
measured_depth.R_f_definition: spec_ids in the family with status `implemented`
measured_depth.R_a_definition: spec_ids in the family with status `implemented` AND admissible is true AND path is not P2

findings.M3-e: R_f 1, R_a 0. M3.6 `leading dim not aligned to descriptor granularity` ships 8 operators but is declared `admissible: false` with prohibition `absent`, so alignment currently has operators and no test. This is a coverage hole that the R_f-only view reports as a healthy 1.
findings.M4-d: R_f 1, R_a 0 by design -- it is the declared noop control, so its instances must be inadmissible for the admissible floor to mean anything.
findings.M3-h: R_f 0 with its only declaration on P2, so the family is unrealisable as declared rather than merely unwritten.

spec_status.note: Defect D2, CORRECTED 2026-09-17. The originally recorded premise was FALSE and is retracted: it claimed that under the two-value enum an `unwritten` spec emits no spec record, so its N/A verdict has nothing to hang on. It does emit one -- `choreo/collect.py::from_spec_registry` walks every entry in the registry snapshot (73 today) and copies `status` through verbatim, so all 23 unwritten specs are represented. Measured cross-tabulation of (status, admissible): implemented/True 45, implemented/False 5, pending/False 23, pending/True 0. Adding a third enum value would therefore unblock nothing: no writer of a new W1 spec needs it. The real defect is a name collision, not a missing value -- `pending` denotes TWO different sets in choreo/mutations.py: the enum value means 'no operator exists' (23 specs), while `pending_specs` -- the GATE 2 list, and the set PATCH-v2.1.md used to gloss as 'admissible, unwritten' -- means 'no operator exists AND admissible' (0 specs). A reader who greps `pending` finds 23 where the gloss promised 0, and `gen_mutants.py --fail-on-pending` reports success without covering 23 of the 23 unwritten specs. Resolution: the gloss in PATCH-v2.1.md is corrected to 'no operator exists; says nothing about admissibility', and mutations.py exports `admissible_unwritten_specs` as an alias of `pending_specs` so a report can state which question it answered. The enum is NOT extended and `pending` is NOT renamed: renaming an existing value would silently change the meaning of every record already written (the `L` -> M3 non-additive hazard) for no gain.
